pass 2026-07-26T10:45:05.130Z · generated 2026-07-26T10:46:30.641Z

Every field of every raw entity in one pass, as it was returned — unknown keys included. Nested objects are recursed into as dotted paths. null is treated as a value and appears in the frequency tables like any other; absent (the key is missing entirely) is counted separately, because upstream uses the two to mean different things. Fields are grouped by what they turned out to be: an invariant has nothing to model, an enum is a value set we can rely on, an opaque field is one only shape describes.

An array of objects is a set of records, not a value: its elements are analysed at <path>[], and every count under that path is per element — how many SKU rows carry a price, not how many endpoints do. The array itself then reports its lengths and which key sets its elements have.
